name: PT Astra International Tbk

frontmatter.title: Astra International: the parts are at the peer discount floor, and the return no longer clears the bar
frontmatter.summary: Results update for the quarter to 30 September 2026. Nine-month revenue was IDR243.87tn and clean profit IDR24.57tn, flat on the prior year. We move the holdco discount to the peer-set floor, normalise the financing mark for the first-half provisioning pace, correct the payout, cost and minority inputs and add parent leases to the bridge; the expected return is 4.0%, so we move to HOLD at Rp4,466.
thesis: The parts are worth Rp4,191 after a 30% discount, the floor of the covered-conglomerate peer set, and the market already prices a 21.8% discount; the base assumes no narrowing [S0, S15].

At Rp4,680 the expected total return is 4.0% including Rp400 of dividends, below the 14.8% cost of equity and below the house ADD hurdle, so the rating is HOLD rather than an ADD on a cost-of-equity roll [S15, S0].

The operating blocks still earn above the cost of equity, but the financing arm is carried at a normalised premium to book after the first-half provisioning pace, and the two listed commodity stakes stay on market marks [S5, S14, S15].

The tabulated bear at Rp3,886 is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity; a true bear that reprices the commodity stakes and marks the financing book at book is lower, which is why the bear carries 30% weight and is not presented as the floor [S14, S5].
The prior valuation kills and the 30 October discard are reconciled: the shares have run to honest marks, and there is no dated discount-narrowing catalyst to underwrite a higher rating [S8, S14].

catalysts.event: Astra voluntary tender offer for Astra Otoparts closes
FY2026 audited results, final dividend and buyback-execution disclosure

frontmatter.catalyst_note: No dated discount-narrowing catalyst exists. The Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised and on-going but has no disclosed end date or pace [S8, S14, S16]; the dated capital-allocation event is the Otoparts tender close on 11 November 2026, which lifts an already consolidated stake rather than upstreaming value to the holdco [S13, S14]. The 30 April 2027 audited-results date dates disclosure, not action. The base therefore assumes no narrowing, the bull discount is capped at the card floor of 20%, and the rating is HOLD.

blocks.text: **The September-quarter results.** Nine-month revenue was IDR243.87tn and clean profit IDR24.57tn, both essentially flat on the prior year, while the reported profit of IDR21.60tn carries the IDR2.96tn non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge [S15, S14]. The third quarter improved on the preceding quarters on mining-contract volumes, the Martabe restart and continued automotive growth, and management guides the fourth quarter to continue on those drivers [S14].

**What changed, and why the rating moves.** The red team showed the ADD did not survive its own arithmetic. The 30% discount was the narrowest in the covered set with no non-circular benchmark, the financing premium ignored the first-half provisioning pace, the payout was the parent cash ratio and the bridge omitted parent leases [S0, S6, S15]. We now hold the discount at the peer-set floor, normalise the financing return, carry the nine-month cost ratio and a minority take near the audited level, set the payout at the company-reported ratio and deduct parent net debt including leases [S4, S6, S15]. The target is Rp4,466 against Rp4,680, a 4.0% expected total return including Rp400 of dividends, and a **HOLD** rating [S15, S0]. The return is below the 14.8% cost of equity, so the old ADD-on-the-roll framing no longer holds.

**The variant view.** The market prices a 21.8% discount on our marks and the shares sit at the wide end of their book history [S0, S15]. We do not dispute that the group is cheap against its parts; we dispute that the gap is a twelve-month return. The discount is sticky, the only named narrowing action is an undated buyback, and upstream cover is comfortable only before parent costs [S6, S8]. The operating blocks still earn above the cost of equity, but that is the base case, not the opportunity [S14]. The prior kills and the 30 October discard are consistent: the stock needs a catalyst that is not dated.

Astra International is a listed portfolio of subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates spanning vehicles, heavy equipment, mining, plantations, toll roads, IT and property [S2]. From the first half of 2026 it reports Automotive, Financial Services and Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment as its three Core Businesses, with everything else in Others [S2, S3].

On the audited FY2025 basis, parent net income split as follows: Automotive & Mobility IDR11.37tn, Financial Services IDR8.95tn, Heavy Equipment, Mining, Construction & Energy IDR9.10tn, Agribusiness IDR1.17tn, Infrastructure IDR1.26tn, Information Technology IDR0.21tn and Property IDR0.72tn [S4]. Automotive is distribution and retail finance on Toyota, Daihatsu, the Honda motorcycle joint venture and Otoparts; Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment is United Tractors, the largest earnings-volatility source [S4].

Strategy changed in 2026: a May roadmap focused the group on three core businesses, put wider businesses under an earn-or-reallocate test, and tied leadership incentives to total shareholder return [S11]; in July shareholders approved a buyback and a management share plan [S8]. Control sits with Jardine Cycle & Carriage Ltd at 50.1% of the shares, part of the Jardine Matheson group, with a 43.0% free float [S6, S0].

The Indonesian car market is the swing factor. National car sales fell through 2025, when the company said its share could reach 51.0% [S4]. They turned hard in 2026: national wholesales reached 679,000 units in the first nine months while Astra's own car sales grew more slowly and its share normalised to 49.0% [S14, S7]. The industry body expects the 850,000-unit full-year target to be met [S7], and industry observers put the realistic range at 890,000 to 930,000 units, above that target [S9]. The recovery is incomplete: middle-income buyers and financing access remain constraints [S9]. Motorcycles are the steadier franchise, with Honda holding 77.0% of the market [S14].

The mining complex is the mirror image, and the third quarter marked a turn. Over nine months Komatsu unit sales fell to 3,000 units and overburden removal to 766.0 million bank cubic metres as the coal quota cut mining customers' capital spending; coal sales fell to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales to 54,000 ounces after Martabe stopped producing [S14]. But the division's attributable profit rose year on year in the third quarter as contract volumes recovered and Martabe restarted [S14]. This is a policy-driven cycle in a business Astra controls through UNTR.

Toyota and Daihatsu retain the leading car brands and Honda is close to a monopoly in motorcycles, while the distribution-and-financing network raises switching costs and gives the financial arm a captive origination channel [S2, S4]. The threat is Chinese entrants and electrified models, which the group meets through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform [S9]. The heavy-equipment moat is Komatsu distribution plus the Pamapersada contractor, tied to the coal cycle [S2].

The state sets the coal quota and vehicle taxes and subsidies shape the car market [S14, S9]. The house macro deck carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar for FY2027E, the policy rate at 5.75 per cent and inflation at 3.3% [KB macro deck, 2026]; the desk carries Indonesian rate-sensitive demand on AVOID.

FY2025 profit before tax was IDR49,288.0bn against EBIT of IDR38,665.0bn, a gap mainly IDR9.62tn of equity-accounted Honda and Toyota income plus other non-operating items; net income was IDR32,769.0bn and earnings per share Rp815 [S6].

Nine-month revenue of IDR243.87tn was flat and gross profit of IDR52.01tn slightly lower [S15]. That is below FY2025 on the Martabe outage and coal-quota hit; the third quarter ran at a materially better margin as mining and gold recovered [S14]. Selling expenses of IDR10.41tn and administrative expenses of IDR16.94tn rose faster than revenue, so operating profit fell [S15].

Reported net profit was IDR21.60tn, but IDR2.96tn of the fall came from non-recurring impairment and fair-value adjustments on equity investments [S14]. Profit before tax was IDR30.01tn; other income turned to an expense of IDR2.43tn from income a year earlier, and joint-venture results rose to IDR8.13tn [S15]. Clean net profit was IDR24.57tn, down about one per cent, with clean earnings per share slightly higher on the smaller share count [S14].
The data pack carries no depreciation line, so we restate it from the audited notes: IDR17.87tn in FY2025 and IDR16.70tn in FY2024 [S6]; FY2025 EBITDA was IDR56,536.0bn, a margin of 17.5% [S6].

Operating cash flow was IDR28.61tn, above consolidated profit even as financing receivables grew [S15, S14]. Capex was IDR17,440.0bn in FY2025 and ran lower in the first nine months; parent dividends paid were IDR16,426.0bn [S15, S0, S6]. The company reports a 48.0% payout ratio on the proposed FY2025 dividend [S4], the ratio used here; the higher parent cash payout mixes dividend income and one-off items [S6].

Group net debt was IDR56,315.0bn at FY2025 [S0], but almost all sits inside the financing subsidiaries, whose net debt was IDR66.70tn [S14]. Excluding them the group had net cash of IDR1.80tn [S14], lower after the Arafura acquisition inside United Tractors' mark [S15, S14]; parent equity rose to IDR238.10tn [S15]. The parent received IDR18.99tn and paid IDR16.43tn in dividends while carrying G&A of IDR4.52tn [S6]: gross upstream cover is comfortable, but net of parent costs it is inadequate.

**Actual versus forecast.** The nine-month actual sets the roll: revenue of IDR243.87tn and clean profit of IDR24.57tn compare with FY2026E forecasts of IDR329,859.8bn and IDR33,081.7bn [S15, S14]; the fourth quarter needs only the third quarter's run-rate, which management guides to on mining volumes, the Martabe restart and automotive growth [S14]. We carry FY2026E revenue growth at 2.0% and the gross margin at 21.7%, the actual plus a fourth-quarter run-rate [S15, S0]. Costs stay at 11.1% of revenue, giving operating profit of IDR34,899.2bn and an EBITDA margin of 16.1% [S15, S14]. From FY2027E the gross margin returns to the FY2025 audited rate while costs stay at the sourced nine-month 11.2% [S15, S6]. Other income is the clean nine-month run-rate annualised at IDR11,548bn. The minority take is 11.0% this year, then rises toward the FY2025 audited IDR7,436.0bn of IDR40,205.0bn as mining recovers, at 18.0% long run [S15, S0]. Net income to the parent is IDR33,081.7bn clean, then IDR33,231.9bn in FY2027E and IDR39,717.6bn by FY2030E [S15, S6].

Earnings-quality flags, run at both levels. **Accruals** are clean: operating cash flow exceeded net profit in FY2023-FY2025 [S0] and again over nine months at IDR28.61tn [S15]. **Non-recurring items** are optics-class: the IDR2.96tn charge is disclosed, non-cash and tied to equity investments; we strip it before the primary SOTP, while the own-history P/E cross-check is on reported LTM and understates clean earnings [S14, S0]. **Margin and cost divergence**: costs grew while revenue was flat, and we hold the nine-month ratio rather than banking operating leverage [S15]. **Financing-book provisioning**: the charge was built, not released, at IDR1.16tn in the first half while receivables grew to IDR132.00tn; we normalise the financing mark for that pace [S5, S14]. **Related-party gravity**: purchases were IDR84.94tn in FY2025, down from 32.8% the year before, and sales IDR27.94tn [S6]. The flows are principally the Toyota, Daihatsu and Honda joint ventures and the ratio fell while the gross margin held; but a transfer-pricing test is not possible, so it is structural but untested [S6]. **Auditor** and **IDX notation** remain open checks: no adverse notice appears in the archive, but we could not verify the board status [S6]. **Fixed-asset revaluation** was immaterial at IDR0.00tn, and no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement was found [S6].

This is a holding company with listed and unlisted parts, so the industry method set applies: a sum-of-the-parts carrying 96% of the weight, cross-checked by own-history earnings and book multiples at 2% and 2% [S0].

The cost of equity is 14.8% and WACC 11.9%, built from a risk-free rate of 7.4% less the sovereign spread of 1.6%, a levered beta of 1.34 (unlevered 0.90, geared for debt-to-market-capitalisation of 0.63) and a mature-market risk premium of 4.2% plus country risk of 2.5% [S0].

The primary method is a look-through sum of the parts. The listed stakes — United Tractors at the effective post-buyback 62.1%, Astra Agro Lestari at 79.7% and Astra Graphia at 76.9% — go in at market [S6]. The unlisted blocks use section-level marks, not one blanket conglomerate multiple [S0, S2]: auto on the blend of Astra Otoparts' and Selamat Sempurna's market earnings multiples; infrastructure on the toll-road card's own-history multiple; property on the listed-property peer median applied to recurring earnings after stripping the IDR0.46tn bargain-purchase gain [S6, F29]. Auto and financial services use nine-month attributable income, IDR9.79tn and IDR7.15tn [S15]. The financing block is on its own book/ROE-COE card: the income includes the segment's joint-venture results, so the book includes joint-venture investments of IDR9.28tn against segment liabilities of IDR97.84tn [S15]. We normalise the annualised return for a fourth quarter at the first-half provisioning pace; on that base the block earns above the 14.8% cost of equity and is carried at a justified premium, while a repeat first-half-size charge would take the return to the cost of equity and the mark to book [S5, S14, F35, F60]. The bridge deducts parent-entity net debt — short-term borrowings of IDR5.05tn against cash of IDR2.64tn plus current and non-current lease liabilities of IDR0.06tn and IDR0.36tn [S15]; group net cash excluding the financing subsidiaries of IDR1.80tn sits inside the marks [S14]. Parent G&A is not capitalised separately: the parent is an operating distributor, so its G&A sits inside the auto mark [S15].

Two listed holdings sit inside earnings blocks rather than at market. Astra Otoparts is a listed minority inside the consolidated auto block; its market multiple is close to the section multiple and the disclosure does not split its income out, so marking the stake separately would double count it [S0, S15]. The majority-owned PT Mega Manunggal Property is consolidated inside the property block; no MMP data pack is in coverage, so it is marked on the same recurring-earnings basis [S6]. The effect is small against the parts.

The cross-checks sit above the primary method: the P/E gives Rp5,425 and P/BV Rp6,686, respectively 29.4% and 59.5% above the sum-of-the-parts [S0]. They diverge because they are undiscounted while the parts carry a 30% discount, because P/BV uses the 30 September 2026 book value of IDR238.10tn [S15], and because the averages were struck when mining earned far more — H1-2025 mining profit was IDR4.98tn against IDR0.61tn a year later [S5]. The own-history multiples carry only nominal weight, and the P/E is on reported LTM earnings including the charge [S0, S14].

**Target construction.** The target is the blended mark of Rp4,265 compounded at the 14.8% cost of equity and net of the Rp400 of dividends paid over the twelve months, which gives Rp4,466 [S15, S0]. There is no discount-convergence term: the target uses the same 30% discount, so the expected return is the cost of capital less the dividend, not a re-rating.

Solving for the discount that reproduces Rp4,680, the market prices a 21.8% discount to our marks [S14, S2] — narrower than the 30% we hold, so the target assumes no convergence. That 30% is the floor of the covered peer set, which has a median materially above it (house coverage) [S0]. ASII's scale and liquidity justify the low end, but net upstream cover is inadequate and the related-party flow untested, so there is no case for going below the floor [S6, S15]. The shares are below their four-year book range, at today's 0.8x against an average of 1.1x [S0], but P/B conflates return on equity with the holdco discount. The only named catalyst is an undated buyback [S8], so the base assumes no narrowing.

The base mixes offsetting departures. Conservative are the peer-floor discount, zero buyback after FY2027E, terminal growth below nominal GDP and capex at the FY2025 top of the range [S0, S6]. Optimistic are the auto block's nine-month annualisation, justified by fourth-quarter guidance [S14], and the minority take just below the audited level. The corrections here remove the prior optimism on cost, payout and financing, leaving the stack close to neutral [S15, S4, S5].

The scenario spread is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity on today's marks. The engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at sourced actuals, so the table does not reprice United Tractors, Astra Agro Lestari or the financing book: the bear transmits through a wider discount, lower revenue and margin, and a higher share count [S8, S14]. We do not present the tabulated bear as the floor. A true bear that also marks the financing arm at book and reprices the two listed commodity stakes below market would be lower; we carry that tail by giving the bear 30% weight, and even the tabulated bear leaves the rating below ADD [S5, S14, F35].

**Regulatory and commodity risk — high likelihood, material impact.** The state sets the coal quota and taxes and subsidies shape the car market; Astra controls neither lever [S14, S9]. Coal, gold, nickel and palm oil all run through earnings, and mining is the most volatile block [S4, S14].

**Macro and currency risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The house desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar for FY2027E and is cautious on Indonesian rate-sensitive demand; a consumer-financing group is exposed on demand and credit [S2, S4]. The caution sits in the 30% bear probability, the country risk premium in the 14.8% cost of equity, and a normalised financing premium.

**Competitive and technology risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** Chinese entrants and electrified models threaten the auto franchise, which meets them through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform; a share or mix loss is the largest value risk [S9, S14].

**Credit and provisioning risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The financing block is IDR66.70tn of net debt against a receivables book of IDR132.00tn and grew new financing to IDR92.50tn. The IDR1.16tn first-half provisioning charge is the trend we watch: a repeat full year at that rate would cut the block's return to the cost of equity and the mark to book. The base normalises for the first-half pace; the stress to book is the named downside, and the holdco template does not reprice the financing mark in a scenario [S5, S14, F35].

**Governance and control risk — high likelihood, structural impact.** Jardine Cycle & Carriage holds 50.1%; no value-unlocking transaction can happen without the controller, and a buyback raises its proportional interest as the float shrinks [S6, S8]. The discount can widen while holders wait, so the base holds it at the peer floor and the bull carries the narrowing.

**Liquidity and dividend risk — low.** The shares turn over IDR243.6bn a day, the parent received more in dividends than it paid in FY2025, and the interim held at the prior year's level [S0, S6, S10]; a deeper mining downturn would pressure it.

The base case (45%) carries the actual nine months: revenue 2.0% this year and 5.0% thereafter, the nine-month cost ratio, a minority take near the audited level, the discount at 30% with no narrowing, and buyback retirement at the completed pace [S14]; it gives Rp4,498. The bull case (25%) assumes the market reaches the observers' range [S9], mining stabilises, wider-business reallocation adds earnings, and the buyback narrows the discount to the card floor, with the Otoparts tender and the Others run-rate above the table [S8, S13, S14, F71, F89]; it gives Rp5,106. The bear case (30%) assumes coal and palm oil weaken, the quota stays tight, credit costs rise, auto share is lost, the buyback stops and the discount widens to the top of its range; it gives Rp3,886, below the price [S14, S8].

Signposts that would change our view: a wholesale run-rate consistent with the observer range while Astra's share holds [S7, S9]; Komatsu and mining-contractor volumes extending the third-quarter improvement [S14]; a dated buyback execution schedule or capital-allocation action on wider businesses [S8, S11]; disclosed buyback execution [S8]; and any deterioration in upstream dividend coverage after parent costs [S6].

Jardine Cycle & Carriage held 50.1% at the last audited date, part of the Jardine Matheson group; the free float is 43.0% [S6, S0]. No pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement is disclosed, and minorities have no route to a control event; the route to value is the dividend, the buyback and the controller's decisions [S6, S8, S11].

Related-party purchases were IDR84.94tn in FY2025 and sales IDR27.94tn, principally the Honda, Toyota and Daihatsu joint ventures [S6]. The purchase ratio fell from 32.8% the year before while the gross margin held, consistent with operating architecture, but the consolidated accounts do not permit a transfer-pricing test; we classify the flow as structural and untested, a discount-widening fact rather than a clean bill [S6].

Capital actions are the main governance signal. The group completed IDR10.00tn of buybacks to September 2026, and the IDR8.00tn Astra programme approved in July is still running with no disclosed end date [S14, S16]. Astra is also offering for up to 4.95 per cent of Astra Otoparts at Rp3,600 a share, lifting its stake to 84.95 per cent, a maximum transaction value of IDR0.86tn [S13, S14]; that is a cash outlay inside an already consolidated block, and whether it adds value depends on the offer price against AUTO's market price, not in our pack, so we do not value it separately [S14, S13]. The board has independent commissioners and a separate audit committee [S6].

Dividends per share were Rp650, Rp519, Rp406 and Rp390 across the last four years [S0], with a Rp98 interim for FY2026 at the prior year's level [S10] and a company-reported 48.0% payout ratio [S4]. On ESG, the material exposures are coal, palm oil and nickel, and the vehicle transition risk, met through its Japanese partners rather than a platform it owns [S14, S9].

The dated catalysts are the monthly wholesale data, the Otoparts tender close in November, and the FY2026 audited results in the spring, when buyback execution must be disclosed [S7, S14, S4]; the October interim was held at the prior year's level despite the profit fall [S10]. None of these is a dated discount-narrowing catalyst, which is why the base does not assume convergence and the rating is HOLD [S8, S14].

Between updates we monitor five things: national car wholesales and Astra's share against the observers' range [S7, S9, F86]; Komatsu units and overburden for evidence the quota downturn has troughed [S14]; net cash excluding financing subsidiaries and parent leases [S14, S15]; buyback execution against the authorised amount [S14, S8]; and parent dividends received against dividends paid and parent costs [S6].

bear.narrative: The national RKAB coal quota stays tight and coal prices fall, so the mining complex does not recover: over nine months Komatsu units were already down 17% to 3,000, overburden down 7% to 766 million bcm, coal sales down 23% to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales down to 54,000 oz after the Martabe stoppage [S14, F53, F54, F55, F56]; H1-2026 mining attributable profit of Rp607bn compares with Rp4,982bn in H1-2025 [S5, F30, F77]. Financial-services credit costs rise as a rate-sensitive CAUTIOUS macro lifts arrears: the financing book carried a Rp1,160bn H1 provisioning charge against Rp132.0tn of receivables and Rp66.7tn of net debt [S5, S14, F35, F51, F60]. The auto franchise loses share and mix to Chinese and electrified entrants [S9], the buyback stops so the share count drifts up, and the holdco discount widens to 40%, the top of the card's persistent 20-40% range, as the buyback fails to close it [S8, S14]. The holdco_sotp engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at their sourced actuals in every case, so the tabulated bear is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity: a true bear that also marks the financing arm at book and reprices United Tractors and Astra Agro Lestari below their market marks would be below the figure shown here, which is why the bear carries 30% weight rather than being presented as the floor.

bull.narrative: The auto market reaches GAIKINDO's 850,000-unit target and industry observers' 890-930k range [S7, S9, F25, F86], with Astra holding about half of it [S4], the national coal quota resets and the mining complex stabilises (this is a bull assumption, not in the base), the Martabe restart and the wider-business reallocation roadmap add earnings - nine-month Others attributable profit was already Rp2,558bn, up 36% [S11, S14, F71] - share gains and a richer mix lift the auto margin, and the ongoing Rp8tn buyback plus the capital-allocation framework narrow the holdco discount to 20%, the floor of the card's persistent range [S8, S14, S11]. The share-count shock carries the buyback acceleration; the Otoparts tender (maximum about Rp858bn [S13, F89]) and the Others run-rate sit above the table because the consolidated marks already carry their earnings. As in the bear, the engine does not reprice the listed stakes or the financing mark in this case, so a re-rating of United Tractors or Astra Agro Lestari would add to the tabulated bull.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at +2%: the nine-month actual was Rp243,869bn [S15] and the third quarter alone Rp85,956bn, ahead of the second quarter's Rp79,245bn; management guides the fourth quarter to be supported by the same drivers that lifted the third - mining-contract volumes, the Martabe restart and continued automotive growth [S14]. A fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate gives full-year revenue of about Rp329.8tn, or +2% on FY2025. The 2% is therefore the last actual and the company's guided continuation, not a step-up beyond it. From FY2027E a 5% nominal growth, below the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation [KB macro deck] but above the old 4% - the auto franchise is recovering and the group now reports three core businesses [S2].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 21.70%, the full-year rate implied by the nine-month actual (gross profit Rp52,008bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, 21.3%) plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's 22.75% (gross profit Rp19,556bn on revenue Rp85,956bn) [S15, S0]; the first half was depressed by the Martabe gold-mine outage and the RKAB coal quota, both of which eased in the third quarter [S14]. From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited 22.09% (gross profit Rp71,444bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S6]), which reproduces the third-quarter exit run-rate rather than the disrupted first half.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11.12% of full-year revenue, and the build is explicit: the nine months are the actual, selling and general expenses of Rp27,353bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, or 11.22% of nine-month revenue [S15], and the fourth quarter is taken at the third quarter's 10.84% rate as promotional spend normalised, so the year blends to 11.12% of full-year revenue rather than the bare 11.22% nine-month ratio. The prior 10.14% FY2025 ratio no longer describes the run-rate. From FY2027E held at the sourced nine-month 11.22% [S15]: the nine-month cost ratio is the last full actual, the third quarter alone (10.84%) is the best quarter and is not the run-rate, and no sourced cost programme justifies reverting to the pre-2026 10.14% ratio. The forecast therefore carries the higher nine-month run-rate, not the best quarter.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of Rp17,871bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn from the audited expenses-by-nature note [S6] (the data pack carries no depreciation line for IDX filers); held flat, with capex at the same years level so the fixed-asset base is stable. H1-2026 D&A was Rp8.7tn on Rp157.9tn of revenue, in line [S5].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual, capex Rp17,440bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S0]; the group reported H1-2026 capital expenditure of Rp5.2tn on a cash basis, Rp6.4tn including leased assets and concession rights [S5], against Rp8.2tn in H1-2025 [S3], so the FY2025 ratio is at the top of the recent range and is not raised.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at zero: the segment note shows consolidated net debt of Rp73.0tn at 30 June 2026, of which Rp67.0tn sits in the financial services segment that funds itself against its own receivables book, and the non-financial segments are net of only Rp6.0tn [S5]; no new group funding is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E rebuilt from the clean nine-month actual, not a rounded-up run-rate: share of joint-venture results was Rp8,127bn for nine months, up from Rp6,769bn a year earlier [S15], and other (expenses)/income net was a Rp2,429bn expense that includes the Rp2,963bn non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge [S15, S14]; adding that charge back leaves about Rp534bn of clean other income, so clean nine-month other non-operating income is Rp8,127bn + Rp534bn = Rp8,661bn [S15, S14]. Annualising the nine months at 4/3 gives Rp11,548bn, which is the FY2026E anchor (no unsourced fourth-quarter step-up). From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited Rp10,702bn (profit before tax Rp49,288bn less EBIT Rp38,665bn plus finance costs Rp3,734bn less interest income Rp3,655bn [S6]), the joint-venture anchor, so the elevated 2026 JV print is not capitalised into the long run. A JV-income shock is carried in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11%, the full-year rate implied by the actual nine months plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's minority take: clean consolidated profit was about Rp27,036bn (reported Rp24,073bn plus the Rp2,963bn non-recurring charge) with about Rp2,471bn to non-controlling interests, a 9.1% clean take [S12, S14, S15]; the third quarter alone carried Rp1,660bn to minorities on Rp10,729bn of profit, a 15.5% take, as United Tractors' mining recovery lifted the 40.5% minority share [S0, S15]. A fourth quarter at that rate gives a full-year take of about 11%. The mining business collapsed in the first half while the wholly owned automotive and financing blocks grew, so the three-year-average 21.4% take is not the 2026 path. From FY2027E the take rises to 17% and 18% long run, close to the FY2025 audited 18.5% (non-controlling interests of Rp7,436bn on Rp40,205bn of consolidated profit [S0]): the base has mining recovering (gross margin back to the FY2025 audited rate and revenue growing), so a mining recovery must lift the minority share toward - not away from - the last audited level. The wholly owned auto and financing mix keeps the long-run take just below that 18.5% actual, not at the 15% used before, which assumed the mining recovery accrued disproportionately to the parent. The UNTR-recovery sensitivity sits in the bear/bull shocks on revenue, margin and share count.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Set at the company-reported FY2025 payout ratio of 48% on the proposed Rp390 per share total dividend [S4, F90], not the 50% parent-entity cash payout (Rp16,426bn of parent cash dividends over FY2025 parent net profit [S6]) that was used before: the 48% is the policy ratio the company itself states, and the 50% is a parent-entity cash-flow ratio that mixes parent dividend income and one-off items. The same Rp98 interim was declared for FY2026 [S10], so the policy is being held, not raised.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at -1.3%: nine-month EPS fell 11% to Rp541 while parent net profit fell 12%, implying a weighted-average share count about 1.3% lower year on year after the group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks between November 2025 and September 2026 [S14]. FY2027E set at -2.0%: the Rp8tn Astra programme approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised, on-going and undated [S8, S14, S16], so rather than assume zero retirement we carry it at the only sourced pace - the Group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks over the eleven months to September 2026 [S14, F65]. At that rate about half of the authorised amount could retire within FY2027E, roughly 2% of the share count at the current price. We stop after one year rather than assume completion, because no end date or pace is disclosed; any residual and any acceleration stay in the bull case. FY2028E onward is held at zero and the completed to-September retirement is already in the FY2026E share count [S14].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 4%, below the house IDR terminal cap of 5% and below the macro deck's implied nominal growth (5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation); it only feeds the reverse-DCF and the cross-checks, as the primary SOTP method carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 30%, the floor of the observed covered-conglomerate peer set and the low end of the 20-40% persistent range the holdco method card makes the base rate. The peer set: ABMM 68.9%, DSSA/TOBA/BHIT 40%, BNBR 38%, ADRO/BRPT/CUAN/FOLK 30%, IMJS 60% (house coverage, CONGLOMERATES). ASII is the largest and most liquid name in that set with a 50.11% Jardine controller, a 42.95% free float and a gross dividend-upstream cover above one [S6, S15, S0], which justifies the low end rather than the 38-40% median; but the net upstream cover after parent G&A is below one and the 29.83% related-party purchase ratio is untested, so there is no sourced case for going below the peer floor. The market-implied discount on our marks is narrower, but it is derived from the same marks and is therefore not an independent benchmark. The base does NOT assume narrowing: the expected return is the cost-of-equity roll plus the dividend, and the only named narrowing catalyst is the Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM and still ongoing, which is authorised but undated [S8, S14, S11]; narrowing is in the bull case only, capped at the card's 20% floor.

challenges.challenge: The tabulated bear (Rp3,928) is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity that leaves the three largest value blocks untouched: UNTR at market (Rp54,248bn, 22.4% of gross SOTP), AALI at market (Rp14,569bn, 6.0%) and the finserv mark (Rp66,527bn, 27.4%) do not move; the bear narrative says coal/palm weaken and credit costs rise but the table holds those marks. The report itself concedes a commodity reprice or provisioning below COE would take value below 3,928, so the bear presented to the reader understates the largest downside and flatters the risk/reward.
challenges.answer: Took the true-bear-range remedy and used it in the weighting. The holdco_sotp engine can shock model inputs but not holding marks, so the tabulated bear is disclosed as a discount-and-earnings sensitivity and the true bear is stated below it: a repeat full H1 provisioning charge takes the financing mark to book (the red team's ~Rp254/share) and a stake reprice adds ~Rp208/share, putting the true bear near Rp3,424 versus the tabulated Rp3,886. The bear probability is raised from 25% to 30% (base 45%, bull 25%) so the weighted target carries the tail; the true-bear-weighted target is still HOLD. The base financing mark is also cut (see C2), so the table no longer carries an unshocked premium.

challenges.challenge: The finserv block (27.4% of gross SOTP) is the most rate/credit-sensitive asset and is carried at 1.178x book on a 16.9% ROE against a 14.8% COE. The report's own credit-risk paragraph says a full year at the H1 provisioning charge (Rp1,160bn against Rp132.0tn receivables) would pull the return to the cost of equity and the premium toward 1.0x, but the scenario table never applies it; the bear's 25% probability and 3,928 TP therefore omit the block's largest identified downside.
challenges.answer: Reduced the base premium and disclosed the unshocked stress. The sustainable ROE is normalised from 16.9% to 16.0% for a fourth quarter at the first-half provisioning pace, so justified P/B falls from 1.178x at the old 14.94% COE to 1.109x at the engine COE of 14.82%, cutting the block from Rp66,527bn to about Rp62,601bn (~Rp99/share before the holdco discount, ~Rp69/share after). A repeat full H1-size charge takes ROE to the COE and the mark to book, the ~Rp254/share stress the red team quantified, and section 5 now states that path explicitly and says the holdco template cannot reprice the holding inside a scenario.

challenges.challenge: The auto (Rp93,973bn), infrastructure (Rp9,059bn) and property (Rp1,836bn) blocks are marked on the group's own 7.2x earnings multiple, i.e. a blanket conglomerate multiple. The VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT card says unlisted segments are valued on their own house card and 'never a blanket multiple', and the same 7.2x is then subjected to a 25% holdco discount, so the discount is counted twice for 44% of gross value. The Honda motorcycle JV (77% share) and the 16.9%-ROE finserv franchise are inside these blanket marks and get no standalone quality premium.
challenges.answer: Replaced the blanket 7.2x with section-level marks: auto on the 7.357x listed-components blend (Astra Otoparts 6.55x and Selamat Sempurna 8.17x LTM), infrastructure on the TOLL_ROADS card's own-history 7.201x because no toll-road data pack exists, and property on the 5.79x listed-property peer median applied to recurring earnings after stripping the Rp464bn bargain-purchase gain. Finserv is on its own P/B card. These are operating-company multiples, so the holdco discount is applied once at the SOTP level, not on top of the group's post-discount P/E. The section marks add about Rp1.7tn to gross value versus the old blanket (auto +Rp2.0tn, property -Rp0.36tn), before the discount change. Parent G&A is not capitalised separately because the parent is itself an operating distributor and its G&A already sits inside the auto earnings mark.

challenges.challenge: The ADD is framed as the 14.8% cost-of-equity roll, but the arithmetic is 12.9% total return: target = 4,601 x 1.1482 - 417 = 4,866, and (4,866 + 417)/4,680 - 1 = 12.9%, because the blended mark (4,601) is below the price (4,680). The report therefore rates ADD on a return 1.9pp below its own COE, and doubling the bear probability to 50% cuts the weighted return to ~7.9%. The 10-29 published rating was ADD at TP 4,849 and 16.1% TR; the price rise has cut the return, yet the ADD is maintained without reconciling to the desk's 30 Oct INDO-ASII DISCARD or the two prior valuation KILLs.
challenges.answer: Moved to HOLD. The house ADD hurdle is an absolute 10% twelve-month total return, not the 14.8% cost of equity, but on the corrected marks the expected return is 4.0% (target Rp4,466 plus Rp400 of dividends against Rp4,680), so it clears neither the ADD hurdle nor the COE and the old ADD-on-the-roll framing is withdrawn. Base probability is now an honest 45% (bear 30%, bull 25%). The investment summary reconciles the two prior valuation kills and the 30 October discard: the shares have run to the honest marks and the twelve-month return needs a dated catalyst that does not exist.

challenges.challenge: The holdco card requires a named and dated discount-narrowing catalyst and says no dated catalyst routes the idea to EVENT_SPECIAL_SIT or passes. The only catalyst is the Rp8tn buyback, which the report itself says has no disclosed end date or pace, and the base explicitly assumes no discount narrowing; catalyst_date 2027-04-30 dates the audited-results disclosure, not the action. The bull then uses a 10% holdco discount, below the card's persistent 20-40% range, without a dated catalyst.
challenges.answer: No dated discount-narrowing catalyst exists, so the idea is reclassified to HOLD and the base assumes no convergence. The bull discount is capped at the card floor of 20% (shock now -10pp from a 30% base, mirrored by the bear at +10pp to 40%), and the 10% outcome is removed because it was unsourced. The nearest dated capital-allocation event is the Astra Otoparts tender close on 11 November 2026, which lifts an already consolidated stake rather than upstreaming value to the holdco; the Rp8tn buyback remains authorised but undated. The frontmatter catalyst date is moved to the tender close and the note says so plainly.

challenges.challenge: The 25% holdco discount is the narrowest in the covered conglomerate group: peers run ABMM 68.9%, DSSA/TOBA/BHIT 40%, BNBR 38%, ADRO/BRPT/CUAN/FOLK 30%, IMJS 60%, median ~34-38%, and the report shows no peer benchmark. At 30% the SOTP falls to ~4,238 and the target to ~4,533 (5.8% return); at 35% to ~4,199 (-1.4%), so the choice is rating-dispositive. The support offered is the market-implied 22.7% discount (derived from the same marks, hence circular) and the P/B history (which conflates ROE and the holdco discount).
challenges.answer: Moved the base discount from 25% to 30%, the peer-set floor: ABMM 68.9%, DSSA/TOBA/BHIT 40%, BNBR 38%, ADRO/BRPT/CUAN/FOLK 30%, IMJS 60%, median around 38-40% (house coverage, CONGLOMERATES). ASII's scale and liquidity justify the low end, but net upstream cover after parent G&A is inadequate and the 29.83% related-party purchase flow is untested, so there is no non-circular case below the peer floor; the market-implied discount is derived from the same marks. At 30% the target is Rp4,466 and TR 4.0%, so the ADD does not stand and the rating is HOLD. At 25% it would be Rp4,866 and 12.9%, which is exactly the unsourced low-end choice the red team identified.

challenges.challenge: The report states dividends paid were 50.0% 'the company describes as its policy ratio' [S15, S0, S4]. S4 actually says the FY2025 payout ratio is 48% on the proposed Rp390 DPS; the 50% is the parent-entity cash payout (Rp16,426bn over parent net profit Rp32,769bn [S6]). The model input uses 50%, so the number is not fabricated, but the attribution to the company is contradicted by the cited source and the 2pp difference changes DPS by ~Rp17.
challenges.answer: Set the payout input to the company-reported 48% on the proposed Rp390 per share FY2025 total dividend [S4, F90]. The 50% is the parent-entity cash payout (Rp16,426bn over parent net profit), a different ratio that mixes parent dividend income and one-off items, and the report now says so. The 2pp change lowers the next-twelve-month DPS by about Rp17.

challenges.challenge: FY2027E opex is set at the third-quarter 10.84% of revenue against the 9M actual 11.22%, i.e. the best quarter, not the 9M average, and the long-run minority take is 15% against the FY2025 audited 18.5% (Rp7,436bn of Rp40,205bn) even though the base has mining recovering. At the 9M opex and FY2025 minority, FY2027E NP parent would be roughly Rp1.9tn lower (~Rp47/share), and the text's claim that the base 'carries the higher run-rate' is not true of the opex line.
challenges.answer: FY2027E opex is now the sourced nine-month 11.22% instead of the best third quarter's 10.84%, and the minority take rises to 17% in FY2027E and 18% long run instead of 15%, close to the FY2025 audited 18.5% as mining recovers. The combined change removes the roughly Rp47/share of optimism the red team quantified; the report text no longer claims the base carries the higher cost run-rate while using the lower one.

challenges.challenge: The bull narrative claims buyback acceleration, the Otoparts tender (80->84.95%, Rp858bn maximum) and wider-business reallocation as upside, but the bull scenario shocks only holdco discount, revenue growth, gross margin and other non-operating income; share_change is fixed at -2.0% FY2027E then zero, and the Otoparts/Others value is not in the 5,803 TP. The same S9 article cited for the middle-income/financing constraints also reports a 890-930k 2026 market forecast, above the 850k target, which is omitted.
challenges.answer: Added a mirrored share-change shock of +/-1.5pp to the bull and bear (replacing the joint-venture shock to stay within the four-shock limit), so the bull carries buyback acceleration and the bear carries a stalled buyback. The Otoparts tender (maximum about Rp858bn) and the Others run-rate are quantified above the table, and the bull discount is capped at the card floor. Added the 890-930k industry-observer range as facts F86/F87 and cited it alongside the 850k target in section 2 and the bull case, so the car-market evidence is two-sided.

challenges.challenge: Three smaller construction inconsistencies: (i) AUTO (~80% of a listed company) and 91.43% of listed MMP sit inside earnings blocks rather than at market, contrary to the card's listed-stakes-at-market rule; (ii) holdco net debt of 2,410 uses only parent short-term borrowings less cash and omits Rp414bn of parent lease liabilities (56 current + 358 non-current) [S15]; (iii) the finserv P/B uses 14.94% COE in the note while the engine COE is 14.82%, and the P/E cross-check uses LTM reported NP of 29,898 including the Rp2.963tn charge despite the text saying the charge is stripped before any multiple [S0, S14].
challenges.answer: Included the Rp414bn of parent lease liabilities (Rp56bn current plus Rp358bn non-current) in holdco net debt, which rises from Rp2,410bn to Rp2,824bn. The financing note now uses the engine COE of 14.82% rather than the stale 14.94%, and the report states that the P/E cross-check is on reported LTM earnings including the non-recurring charge, so it is not a clean multiple. The AUTO and MMP treatments are disclosed: both are consolidated inside earnings blocks, AUTO because its market multiple is close to the section multiple and its income is not split out, MMP because no data pack is in coverage.

challenges.challenge: Several factual claims outrun their citations: the macro-deck rupiah 18,350, BI 5.75% and CPI 3.3% are cited to [S2, S4] which do not contain them; 'more than three hundred subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates' is cited to S2, which has no such number; 'just under twenty-two per cent' gross margin is 21.33% [S15]; the IDX notation/auditor status is an open check, not a verified clean; and the 29.83% related-party purchase ratio in F21 is dismissed as 'operating architecture, not value leakage' without a transfer-pricing test, although the card calls related-party gravity the modal IDX value-destruction channel [S6, F21].
challenges.answer: The macro numbers are now cited to the house macro deck rather than to company sources. The unsourced entity count is removed. The gross-margin claim is removed and replaced by the two source figures, gross profit and revenue. Auditor and IDX notation status are stated as unverified open checks rather than clean. The related-party purchase ratio is tested against the prior year (29.83% versus 32.83%) and the gross-margin trend; it fell while the margin held, but a transfer-pricing test is not possible from the consolidated accounts, so the report calls it structural and untested rather than value leakage.

challenges.challenge: The base mixes conservative and optimistic departures without a net reconciliation: conservative are the 7.2x group multiple plus 25% discount on the unlisted blocks (double discount), zero buyback after FY2027E, 4% terminal growth below nominal GDP, and capex at the FY2025 top of range; optimistic are FY2027E opex 10.84% vs 9M 11.22%, minority 15% vs FY2025 18.5%, payout 50% vs company 48%, auto 9M x 4/3 vs LTM, and the bull's 10% discount outside the 20-40% range. The report does not say which way the stack nets.
challenges.answer: Added a reconciliation paragraph in section 4. Conservative: peer-floor discount, zero buyback after FY2027E, terminal growth below nominal GDP and capex at the FY2025 top of the range. Optimistic: auto nine-month annualisation, justified by management's fourth-quarter guidance, and the minority take just below the audited level. The prior optimism on cost, payout and financing premium is removed, so the remaining stack is close to neutral and the rating does not depend on it.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull TP of 5,803 contains no share-change, Otoparts or wider-business shock: the narrative's buyback acceleration, the 80->84.95% Otoparts tender and the +36% Others run-rate are all above-table [S13, F62, F63, F65, F71], and the base stops share_change at FY2027E. The S9 article is cited for the bearish constraints but its 890-930k 2026 market forecast, above the 850k target, is omitted [S9, S7].

missing_bear_case.note: The tabulated bear holds UNTR (22.4% of gross SOTP), AALI (6.0%) and the finserv book (27.4%) at market or sourced marks, so the largest value blocks have no downside in the table; the report itself says a commodity reprice or provisioning would take value below the 3,928 bear [S14, S5, F51, F60]. The finserv P/B of 1.178x would fall to ~1.0x on a repeat H1 provisioning charge, about Rp254/share, and a 20% UNTR/AALI reprice is about Rp208/share, neither in the bear.

assumption_realism.note: The 25% holdco discount is the lowest in the covered conglomerate peer set (ABMM 68.9%, DSSA/TOBA/BHIT 40%, BNBR 38%, ADRO/BRPT/CUAN/FOLK 30%, IMJS 60%), and no peer benchmark is shown; at 30% the SOTP falls to ~4,238 and the target to ~4,533 (5.8% return), at 35% to ~4,199 (negative), so the discount choice is rating-dispositive [S0]. FY2027E opex of 10.84% is below the 9M actual 11.22%, minority of 15% is below the FY2025 audited 18.5%, and the auto mark uses 9M x 4/3 (13,049) against LTM 12,119 [S15, S6, S14].

evidence_and_citations.note: The report says the 50.0% payout is what the company describes as its policy ratio, but S4 states the FY2025 payout ratio is 48% on Rp390 DPS; 50% is the parent-entity cash payout (16,426/32,769) [S4, S6]. The macro deck's rupiah 18,350, BI 5.75% and CPI 3.3% are cited to [S2, S4], which do not contain them; the 'more than three hundred subsidiaries' claim is cited to S2, which has no such number; the 22.7% implied discount is cited to [S14, S2] although it is an engine output from S0; 'just under twenty-two per cent' is 21.33% [S15].

valuation_method_fit.note: The unlisted auto (38.7% of gross), infrastructure and property blocks (44% combined) are marked on the group's own 7.2x earnings multiple, which the holdco card says should never be a blanket multiple, and the same blocks are then subjected to a 25% holdco discount, double-counting the discount; no holdco opex is capitalized or deducted; the dividend-upstream 1.16x is gross of parent costs; AUTO and 91.43% of MMP are listed stakes not marked at market [S0, S6, F78, F80, F81].

bias_and_tone.note: The ADD is justified as the 14.8% COE roll, but the expected total return is 12.9% (price 4,680 vs blended v0 4,601), 1.9pp below the stated COE; doubling the bear probability to 50% cuts the weighted return to ~7.9%. The report maintains ADD after the TR fell from the 10-29 published 16.1% (TP 4,849) and does not reconcile with the desk's 30 Oct INDO-ASII DISCARD or the two prior valuation KILLs (T-INDO-ASII-001/002) [S0, S14; KB].

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The macro deck is CAUTIOUS and explicitly AVOID on Indonesian rate-sensitive names; the report is ADD on a consumer-discretionary/consumer-financing group and reconciles only generically through the 25% bear probability and the country risk premium, with the deck inputs cited to company sources [S2, S4]. No peer discount or peer multiple benchmark is used, even though the 25% discount is the peer-set low [S0].

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative items: the 7.2x group multiple plus 25% discount on the unlisted blocks, zero buyback after FY2027E, 4% terminal growth below nominal GDP, and the 5.526% capex held at the FY2025 top of range [S0, S6]. Optimistic items: FY2027E opex 10.84% vs 9M 11.22%, minority 15% vs FY2025 18.5%, payout 50% vs company 48%, auto 9M x 4/3 vs LTM, and the bull's 10% discount outside the card's 20-40% range [S15, S4, S14]. The net offset is not reconciled.

calibration.note: cov_engine qc has no BLOCK flags and only the weights.changed WARN, which is justified with [S0, S15]; the FY2025A-to-FY2026E EBITDA-margin gap of -1.38pp is the nine-month cost ratio carried forward and is explained in section 3 [S15, S6]. FY2026E reproduces the 9M actual plus a Q4 at the Q3 run-rate, and the model balances.

signoff.notes: APPROVED — HOLD, target Rp4,466, expected total return 4.0% at Rp4,680 (including Rp400 DPS), COE 14.8% / WACC 11.9%; leave at signoff for the Director to publish. QC round 1 PASS (judge PASS, neutral, no BLOCK); engine blocking none; draft lint PASS. All C1-C12 MATERIAL/MINOR red-team challenges are answered on substance and reflected in the files: the ADD is withdrawn, the discount is at the 30% peer floor with no convergence, the financing mark is normalised for the first-half provisioning pace, payout is the company-reported 48%, FY2027E opex and the minority take are at the sourced nine-month/audited levels, and parent leases are in the holdco bridge. On the corrected arithmetic 4.0% clears neither the 10% ADD hurdle nor the cost of equity, so HOLD is the right call. BATCH/COMPS: CONGLOMERATES calls are mixed (ADD ABMM; HOLD ADRO/ASII/BNBR/IMJS/TOBA; REDUCE BRPT; SELL DSSA/FOLK; plus parked names); the HOLD cluster is not a shared-input tilt — holdco discounts run 30-68.9% and ASII's 30% is the peer-set floor reasoned in C6, while ASII's 11.9% WACC / 14.8% COE is its own beta build, not an identical input. KONGLO-GROUP READ: ASII's listed holdings UNTR (62.12% effective), AALI (79.68%) and ASGR (76.87%) are marked at market; none has house coverage (data-pack only), so the covered-sibling rule is met. BRPT.JK remains at signoff under the Director's ruling and is deliberately not signed here. RESIDUAL NON-BLOCKING QC FIX ITEMS, none affecting HOLD/Rp4,466, to clear before the next version: Q1 restate §4 target construction as base Rp4,498 then probability-weight to Rp4,466; Q2/Q4/Q5 cite the COC inputs and the §5 house view to the macro deck and the 42.95% free float to the IDX registry; Q3 cite house coverage for the peer set and add ASII's own 5y SOTP-discount range (or state it is unavailable); Q6 restate the post-balance-sheet window as since 30 September 2026; Q7 reconcile or footnote the FY2026E net-debt row and state the SOTP uses the parent-entity bridge; Q8 show the true-bear-weighted target (~Rp4,328, TR ~1.0%, still HOLD). NOTEs Q9-Q12 are advice for the same update (related-party % of revenue, IDX notation/auditor open check, weights citation, provisioning-charge definition). CONTAMINATION: none found — no broker rating, target or consensus number in fund record, fund record, fund record, fund record or fund record; peer references are house coverage.

bias.note: The base is anchored on the nine-month actual and management's Q4 continuation: revenue +2% this year, opex at the 11.22% nine-month rate, minority 11% this year and 18% long run, payout at the company-reported 48%, and the discount at the 30% peer floor with no narrowing. Conservative items (capex at the FY2025 top, buyback stops after FY2027E, 4% terminal growth, financing ROE normalised to 16.0%) are offset by optimistic ones (auto 9M annualised at 4/3, minority 11% vs the 18.5% FY2025 audited, 5% FY2027E growth). The stack is close to neutral and does not move the HOLD; the table's bear is disclosed as a sensitivity and the true bear is lower.

recomputed.item: Net cash excluding financial services at 30 Sep 2026

findings.finding: §4 says the Rp4,265 blended mark compounded at the 14.8% COE less Rp400 of dividends gives Rp4,466; the arithmetic gives Rp4,498, which is the base-scenario TP. Rp4,466 is the probability-weighted target (0.45 x 4,498 + 0.30 x 3,886 + 0.25 x 5,106).

The cost-of-capital inputs (rf 7.45%, sovereign spread 1.62%, ERP 4.23%, country risk 2.46%, unlevered beta 0.90) are cited to [S0], but S0 is Yahoo statements/prices/profile and does not contain them; the engine reads them from the house macro deck and config.

§4 cites [S0] for the peer-set discount benchmark (ABMM 68.9%, DSSA/TOBA/BHIT 40%, BNBR 38%, ADRO/BRPT/CUAN/FOLK 30%, IMJS 60%), which is house coverage, not S0; and the report gives no ASII own five-year SOTP-discount range, which the holdco card's output contract requires. The discount choice is rating-dispositive.
The 43.0% free float is cited [S6, S0]. S6 discloses Jardine at 50.11% and treasury shares but not the float; the datapack's 42.95% free float is sourced to the IDX registry via the IDX-IC mirror.
§5 macro and currency risk cites [S2, S4] for the house desk's rupiah 18,350, policy-rate caution and rate-sensitive AVOID view; S2/S4 are company releases and do not contain the house desk view.

valuation.post_bs_review says it searched since the 30 June 2026 balance sheet, but the balance-sheet date is now 30 September 2026; it does cover the 2 October interim and the 13 October-11 November Otoparts tender, and the Arafura acquisition (February 2026) predates both dates.

The model's FY2026E net debt is Rp32,472bn against Rp56,315bn at FY2025 and Rp63,049bn at 30 September 2026, with net_borrowing held at zero; the line implies a roughly Rp30tn fourth-quarter cash build while the financing book is growing. The SOTP bridge uses parent net debt Rp2,824bn and is correct, so the target is unaffected.

§5 says the true bear (financing mark at book, listed stakes repriced) is below the tabulated Rp3,886 bear and that the 30% bear weight carries that tail, but the engine target Rp4,466 weights the tabulated Rp3,886, not the true bear near Rp3,424. A true-bear-weighted target is about Rp4,328 (TR about 1.0%). The rating stays HOLD.

The 29.83% related-party purchase ratio is % of total cost of revenue plus selling and G&A (S6 Note 32b), not % of revenue; the report gives absolute purchases and sales but not the EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS output of related-party flows as % of revenue.
IDX notation/special-monitoring-board and auditor status remain open checks; the EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS card requires the board/notation status to be checked first.
The weights.changed justification cites [S0, S15], which do not discuss method weights; the 96/2/2 choice is supported by the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT card and the red-team record, not those sources.

§5 says a repeat full year at the first-half provisioning rate would cut the financing return to the COE; the arithmetic is a repeat first-half-size charge (Rp1,160bn) in Q4 giving about 14.8%, while a full year at the per-quarter H1 pace (Rp580bn) is the 16.0% base.
